Messages.Author: Jay Kristoff
Messages.Body:
Minion A is bleeding Meth. B. Meth. B plays Telepathic Counter to reduce
the bleed to zero. The bleed is then modified to take the bleed total back
up above zero. At this point can Meth. B attempt to block the action?

In the same scenario, if Meth. B were to bounce the bleed to Meth C, would
Meth. B's Telepathic Counter still reduce the bleed that is now headed at
Meth. C?

If Meth C were then to bounce the bleed back to Meth. B would the initial
Telepathic Counter still be in effect?

thanks,
Jay

Messages.Author: Tom, Mad&Co
Messages.Body:
"Jay Kristoff" <j...@columbus.rr.com> escribió en el mensaje
news:vN3R6.170766$BB5.2...@typhoon.columbus.rr.com...

> Minion A is bleeding Meth. B. Meth. B plays Telepathic Counter to reduce
> the bleed to zero. The bleed is then modified to take the bleed total
back
> up above zero. At this point can Meth. B attempt to block the action?

Yes, if you haven't yet "give up" blocking the bleed. Eventually, it usually
works as follows: A bleeds, B plays TC, A enhances the bleed, B is able to
block, since B hasn'y give up blocking the action.If B stated at some point
that gives up, he won't be able to block it. It's a usual strategy (if you
play with bouncing cards) that you give up blocking minion A, to see if it
enhances it's bleed some way or another, and bounce it after the
Conditioning has been played. The problem is that if Meth C (new target of
the bleed) bounces it against you again, you cannot try to block it anyway,
thought you still can bounce it again with another minion or the same minion
if you play a different bouncing card.

>
> In the same scenario, if Meth. B were to bounce the bleed to Meth C, would
> Meth. B's Telepathic Counter still reduce the bleed that is now headed at
> Meth. C?

It depends. If you reduce it and then you bounce it, yes. If you bounce the
bleed, you cannot reduce it with TC.

Tom Mad&Co

Messages.Author: Tom, Mad&Co
Messages.Body:
"Jack Crow" <no...@nowhere.com> escribió en el mensaje
news:3b14d65c...@news.flrtn1.occa.home.com...

> If I remember right, all action modifiers must be played before
> reaction cards can be played...by the same turn, once a reaction has
> been played, you cannot play action modifiers. Does this mean cards
> that "tap to gain +1 stealth/bleed/whatever" should be treated as
> action modifiers? wow...why do I feel like this is a question about a
> M:TG spell resolution stack?

No, you are not right. You can always play a reaction card after an action
modifier, and the oppossite, whenever someone plays a reaction, you can play
an Action Modifier. Cards that Tap to gain +1 [something] are treated as
action modifiers. And this is not M:TG. Here there are no "instant" or
"interrupt" cards.

A standard bleed action:

Gilbert Duan plays a GtU at inferior (+2 bleed action card). His prey has
anneke tapped, so he plays a 2nd Trad to untap with +2 intercept and attemps
to block. Gilbert Duan plays a Lost in Crowds, and then a Faceless Night,
for a final +3 stealth. Anneke plays a TC to reduce the bleed to 1, and
gives up blocking (the Meth must state it). Gilbert Duan DOM allows him to
play a Conditiong to pump the final bleed to 4. Then anneke should bounce it
with a Telepathic misdirection and the GD ends his action bleeding anneke's
prey for 4.

Hope it's been well explained...

Tom Mad&Co

Messages.Author: Gomi no Sensei
Messages.Body:
In article <vN3R6.170766$BB5.2...@typhoon.columbus.rr.com>,

Jay Kristoff <j...@columbus.rr.com> wrote:
>Minion A is bleeding Meth. B. Meth. B plays Telepathic Counter to reduce
>the bleed to zero. The bleed is then modified to take the bleed total back
>up above zero. At this point can Meth. B attempt to block the action?

Yes, unless B has already declined to block.

>In the same scenario, if Meth. B were to bounce the bleed to Meth C, would
>Meth. B's Telepathic Counter still reduce the bleed that is now headed at
>Meth. C?

Yes. Telepathic Counter requires that the bleed be directed at you
at the time you play it. What happens after that is immaterial; the
reduction is in effect.

>If Meth C were then to bounce the bleed back to Meth. B would the initial
>Telepathic Counter still be in effect?

Yes. It would be in effect for the duration of the bleed action.
